solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Feud, with a charge about to stick

indicators.note: about means the word for charge goes around the word for stick

parts.note: rent is a charge paid for the use of property
gum is a glue, so a thing that makes things stick

explanation.surface: A feud flares up, with someone about to have a charge stick to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a criminal accusation, but it is the money paid for a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A feud is a bitter quarrel, and an argument is a dispute or quarrel.

clue.text: A religious group gathered round piano, look

indicators.note: the group gathers round, enclosing the letter for piano

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
P is the musical abbreviation for piano

explanation.surface: A congregation assembles around a piano to have a look.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is a look or appearance, as in a person's grim aspect.

clue.text: Replacing ear etc — that could be a branch of medicine

indicators.note: says what the rearranged letters could become, a signal to shuffle them

explanation.surface: Swapping out an ear and other parts sounds like a specialism of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replacing' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: General practice is family medicine, the field of the GP or family doctor.

clue.text: Intends to have financial resources

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb: he ... to go
... as a plural noun: money or wealth, living beyond your ...

explanation.surface: Someone plans to get money.
explanation.definitionFit: Means is both a verb for having in mind and a noun for income or wealth.

clue.text: Bits of food — unspecified number? Lots!

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics
oodles means lots

explanation.surface: How many bits of food are there? Lots of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are strips of pasta, pieces of food.

clue.text: After spring left-winger is forgiven

indicators.note: after puts the left-winger's word following the spring's word

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
a red is a socialist or communist, someone on the political left

explanation.surface: Once spring arrives, a left-wing politician is pardoned.
explanation.definitionFit: To be spared is to be let off or pardoned, which is what being forgiven amounts to.

clue.text: Holy woman that is on street beset by crowd

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the crowd encloses the other letters

parts.note: a press is a crowd or throng of people

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A holy woman out on the street is mobbed by a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A priestess is a woman who performs sacred rites in a temple.

clue.text: This county produces whisky: you'd see dry Scotsman roar otherwise!

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teetotal Scotsman would protest loudly about a county famous for whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross and Cromarty is a former county in the Scottish Highlands, home to distilleries such as Glenmorangie and Dalmore.
explanation.definitionFit: The county named is a historic Highland county noted for its distilleries.

clue.text: A hat raised over politician wasting time

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the politician
raised in a down clue means the words are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician dawdles while a hat is lifted above him.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory means slow and given to delay.

clue.text: Something used for writing label on figure

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A pen is used to write a label on a diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' means a geometrical shape here, not a number or a diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagon is a five-sided geometrical shape, a plane figure.

clue.text: Christmas decoration from department in Selfridges

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is taken out of the letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A Christmas decoration bought from a department in Selfridges, the London store.
explanation.walkthrough: Selfridges is a big London department store; the answer runs across the end of 'department', 'in' and the start of 'Selfridges'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is the glittering strands hung on Christmas trees as festive ornament.

clue.text: The old man getting married in ceremony

indicators.note: in puts the letter for married inside the word for father

parts.note: pop is informal for father, the old man

explanation.surface: Dad gets married at a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is grand ceremonial display, as in pomp and circumstance.

clue.text: One body or another seen to be inadequate

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: another body, following 'One body', is a corpse, a dead body

explanation.surface: Of two bodies of people, one is judged not up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on two senses of body: a group of people, and a dead body, CORPSE, which 'seen to be inadequate' cuts short by its last E.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is an organised group of people, such as an army unit, a single body.

clue.text: Organise room with talks — be quick about it!

indicators.note: to organise is to put in order, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: An impatient instruction to get a room ready for talks without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Look smart is an informal British command meaning hurry up.

clue.text: Second-rate security devices in accommodation units?

parts.note: B is the grade below A, so second-rate
locks are devices that keep things secure

explanation.surface: Poor-quality locks fitted in flats or rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a loose definition: blocks of flats house people.
explanation.definitionFit: A block is a large building divided into flats or offices, so a unit of housing.

clue.text: In fact, nod excitedly as one listening to confession?

indicators.note: excitedly suggests agitated motion, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A person nods eagerly while hearing a confession.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that 'confession' is not a church one; a priest wants to be the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidant is a trusted friend to whom secrets are told.

clue.text: Quiet piece by editor who makes an appeal?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
a leader is a newspaper's editorial article, often written by the editor

explanation.surface: A low-key editorial article that makes an appeal to readers.
explanation.walkthrough: A leader is the British word for a newspaper editorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleader is someone arguing a case or begging, the person behind a plea.

clue.text: Done with actors being gloomy

parts.note: over means finished, done
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: Finished with the actors, someone is feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is grey and dull, gloomy weather.

clue.text: A minister goes back — and appears in that porch

indicators.note: the word and is placed inside the reversed letters just made
goes back says the letters of a minister are read in reverse order

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, the title of a church minister

explanation.surface: A clergyman returns and turns up in a porch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' points back at the reversed letters 'goes back' has just made, so the word 'and' sits inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed open gallery along the front of a house, much like a porch.

clue.text: A soldier getting nothing as a fee

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A soldier being paid nothing as his fee.
explanation.walkthrough: Agio is a banking term: a charge for exchanging money.
explanation.definitionFit: Agio is the premium or charge paid when changing currency, a kind of fee.

clue.text: Spy making some in Paris weep

parts.note: des is French for some
to cry is to weep

explanation.surface: A spy in Paris reduces some people to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spy' is a verb, to catch sight of, not a secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To descry is a literary verb meaning to catch sight of something far off.

clue.text: Plant in marsh European, says Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the first sounds of words

parts.note: a bog is a marsh
a Dane is a European, from Denmark

explanation.surface: A plant in a marsh is European, so Spooner says.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first letters of BOG DANE to get DOG BANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogbane is a plant, supposedly poisonous to dogs.

clue.text: Padre troubled about army finally addressed the Almighty

indicators.note: about puts the scrambled letters round the final letter
troubled means disturbed, so the letters are mixed up
finally takes the last letter of the word army

explanation.surface: A worried army chaplain spoke to God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges PADRE into PRAED, and 'about' wraps it round Y, the last of 'army'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray is to speak to God, so prayed is addressed God in the past tense.

clue.text: Shrinking away from girl I once fancied

indicators.note: fancied suggests something imagined or made up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from a girl they once had a crush on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancied' reads as having a crush on, but it is the signal to rearrange GIRL I ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Recoiling is flinching or drawing back in fear or disgust.

clue.text: This writer resides in Russian community? One has nothing to say

indicators.note: resides in puts the writer inside the community

parts.note: a mir was a peasant village commune in Tsarist Russia
the setter calls themself this writer, so ME

explanation.surface: The setter lives in a Russian village where people have nothing to say.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimer is a mime artist, who performs silently without words.

clue.text: Instrument to measure a distance, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the word is one that sounds the same

parts.note: a metre is a unit of length, so a distance

explanation.surface: A device for measuring a distance, so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter is a gauge, a device that records quantities such as gas used.

clue.text: Brute has knocked over plate

indicators.note: knocked over suggests something upended, so the word for plate is read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A thug has sent a plate flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is a beast, an animal as opposed to a human; also a savage person.

clue.text: Wind — see plant being sheltered

indicators.note: being sheltered means the plant sits inside the see's name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see
an aster is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: Beware the wind: look, a plant is being given shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a bishop's diocese, here Ely in Cambridgeshire, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind blowing from the east.

clue.text: The newspaper's illegal acts

parts.note: FT's: the Financial Times, this puzzle's own newspaper, with its possessive

explanation.surface: A newspaper reporting on its own crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Thefts are acts of stealing, crimes against the law.

clue.text: Female with a hint of sunshine in performance will be paid

indicators.note: in puts the female and the ray inside the deed

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
a ray is a single beam, a hint of sunshine

explanation.surface: A woman with a sunny touch to her act is promised her fee.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose on tense: costs defrayed are costs that will be or have been paid.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray expenses is to settle or pay them; defrayed costs are those met.
